analysis: Examined the prompt-contract fixture tail (production_vectors.json, head lines 56733-58328) and the Swift ChatTemplateControls/templateAdditionalContext change in MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine+Translation.swift. The fixture changes are golden-vector data only: provider_body/template_input with fixed fixture-scope and date 2028-02-29, token IDs, and chain hashes. These are regenerated and contain no secrets. The vector changes follow the new rule that JSON response formats render with enable_thinking=false, as seen in the added additional_context in the patch. Prompt-contract IDs and chain hashes feed coordinator-authored cacheSalt and block-hash routing (T-041). The fixtures regenerate consistent vectors, and cache scoping stays keyed by account, model build and prompt-contract ID. The Swift change adds reasoningBudgetTokens and changes promptDate to private(set) var. withPromptDate now copies self, which preserves all raw* evidence fields and removes the risk of a hand-copied field list dropping evidence. A new branch sets enable_thinking=false for JSON response formats on Qwen3.5-family models when the caller gave no thinking control, effort or budget. This only changes prompt rendering, not authorization, encryption, attestation or billing boundaries. Residual questions for integration: (1) the Go coordinator prompt sidecar must mirror this rule exactly, or the plan token counts and chain hashes will diverge from provider rendering, which would degrade cache routing and cause fail-closed mismatches (an availability or correctness concern, not a confidentiality one). That code was not supplied. (2) Where reasoningBudgetTokens is extracted from the raw body is not visible here. Inconsistent extraction on the provider could create a mismatch, but that is not shown to be a security regression. No security regression is identified from the supplied evidence. The excerpt of the fixture patch is truncated, so it is not fully verified line by line.
